test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-1 2021: Official Paper (Held On : 6 June 2022 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: A dishonest dealer is selling sugar at Rs. 40 per kg and pretending that he is selling it at a loss of Rs. 5 per kg but he actually gives 800 g instead of 1 kg, using a faulty weight. What is his actual profit or loss percent?
solution:
Given:- SP = Rs. 40 /kg, used faulty weight and gave 800g in place of 1 kg

To find:- Actual profit and loss percent

Formula used:- % profit = (SP-CP)/(CP)times 100 , Loss % = (CP-SP)/(CP)times 100

Calculation:- It is mentioned in the question that he is pretending to sell a kg of sugar at a loss of Rs. 5 per kg

⇒CP - SP = 5

⇒CP = 45 per Kg (Since, SP = 40 per kg)

As given, he is using faulty weight and gives 800g instead of 1 kg,

Suppose he sells a 1 kg sugar to a customer,

⇒The CP of the 1 kg of sugar = Rs. 45 

But he actually gave 800g to a customer so the cost paid by the dealer to purchase that sugar will be,

⇒ The CP of the 800 kg of sugar = (45)/(1000)times 800 = Rs. 36

Profit % = (SP-CP)/(CP)times 100

Profit % = (40-36)/(36)times 100

\% profit = (100)/(9)

**The actual profit of a dealer is of 11 {1 over 9}%**%.
